newsitem.title: USA: St. Louis sports authority bill before Mo. Senate.
newsitem.headline: St. Louis sports authority bill before Mo. Senate.

text.p: A bill that would create an authority to review and analyze current sports franchises in St. Louis as well as the possibility of franchise expansions in the city is headed to the Missouri Senate floor after a committee approved the measure on Monday.
The bill passed the Senate Corrections and General Laws Committee on Monday and is waiting to be reported to the Senate floor, according to the Senate communications office.
The measure would create a five-member St. Louis Sports Complex Authority that would report annually to the governor on its findings and recommendations.
The bill reportedly grew out of the possibility that the St. Louis Cardinals baseball team may be looking for a new ballpark to replace Busch Stadium in 10 to 15 years.
The team's president has said that the team expects to form a public-private partnership to build a stadium.
